claims.statement: A destination is two methods: notify to show the card, and edit_and_strip to remove whatever invites an answer once the card is closed.
The console destination prints the card fields and the exact command that answers it, with no network call, which is what lets a first run complete the loop with no external service.
The Telegram adapter sends the message first and attaches the inline keyboard by editing it, remembering the message location so a later claim can find it.
The Telegram adapter encodes the card id, the version and the choice into the callback payload, so a button left over from an earlier revision cannot claim anything.
A failed control strip does not fail the answer: the answer is already durable in the store, so a dead destination is an honest miss and a client recovers through the wait or the read.

The served MCP surface is twelve tools: how_to_use, ask_question, request_approval, get_response, list_unprocessed, list_pending, mark_processed, report_execution, update_request, cancel_request, notify_user and request_feedback.

The card payload handed to notify is built in _notification_payload and carries request_id, version, kind, title (the card's question or title, else "Paraphe"), details (its context or details), choices, choice_notes, recommendation, consequence, prohibitions, links, agent_name, risk, expires_at, runtime, repo, worktree and ticket, plus renotify true when a revised card is re-sent.

notify_user reuses the destination seam with a status payload -- kind notify plus title, message, agent_name and risk -- instead of a card, so a destination branches on kind before treating a payload as a card; the console prints one line for it and the Telegram adapter sends it with no keyboard.

Adding a destination is implementing notify and edit_and_strip and injecting the object into the inbox's notifier and tap-port slots: the inbox knows nothing else about it, so a destination cannot change the card lifecycle and the lifecycle cannot require a new method of an existing destination; the only other members the inbox probes for (finalize_message, remember_message) are optional and reached with getattr.

The inbox calls edit_and_strip when a claim lands, when a refusal finds the card already closed, when a card expires, when cancel_request withdraws one, and to retire the revision an update_request superseded.

The composition root, not the inbox, chooses the destination from configuration: a bot token means the Telegram tap adapter wired as both the notifier and the tap port, its absence means the console destination with the null tap port.
The inbox's notifier and tap-port slots default to no-ops (_NullNotifier, NullTelegramPort), so an inbox with no destination wired still serves creates and answers, notifying nobody.

A failing notify rolls back the notification reservation only when the provider proved the send did not happen (NotifyRejected) and no message identity was recorded; otherwise the exception propagates to the caller.
On update_request, a failing strip of the superseded revision writes the previous revision back and propagates, so the store never advertises a revision whose previous message could not be closed.
source_thread is descriptive metadata: the card stores the value the caller sent, and nothing is resumed from it.

There is no delivery seam: a destination never carries the answer back, and the answer returns through the ask itself - the waited call (wait_seconds on ask_question, request_approval and get_response), the paraphe wait command with exits 0 answered and 3 not answerable and 4 unknown, or the get_response / list_unprocessed read - with the durable store as the fallback when a wait is missed.
The Telegram adapter strips stale controls when a callback's message no longer matches the card, for a refusal whose reason is stale_message or stale_version.

tests/inbox/test_surface_contract.py pins the destination contract, with the console implementation's notify and edit_and_strip both running through the printed output, and tests/inbox/test_setup.py pins that the printed card carries the request id, the /answer path and PARAPHE_OWNER_ANSWER_TOKEN.

The notify payload is a curated subset of the card: priority, project, source_thread, external_id, allow_freeform, expires_in_seconds and the lifecycle state stay in the store and the deadline travels as expires_at, so priority is the one entry of the docs/adapters.md field list the inbox never sets and destinations must read optional keys tolerantly, as both shipped implementations do with payload.get.

notify_user never creates a card: it de-duplicates the delivery on external_id through the store's notification-id table, and a NotifyRejected carrying an external_id drops that reservation so a later call sends again.

The destination seam is two independently injected slots: the notifier receives only notify and the tap port only edit_and_strip, so Runtime.start wires the console destination as notifier only while the tap port stays NullTelegramPort and a running console-mode server never calls its edit_and_strip.

The inbox notifies each card revision at most once: its notified reservation is stored before notify is called, so a duplicate create or a restart does not re-send, and only update_request with renotify clears the flag and sends the new revision with renotify true.
At startup, reconcile_notifications strips every card that is no longer open, so a card that closed while the process was down has its controls removed on the next start.

An owner's reply to a card message is recorded as that card's answer -- Inbox.claim_reply with responded_via telegram-reply -- with the same lifecycle writes a tap makes, and a reply to a status message resolves to no card; the reply enters through the adapter and never passes through notify.

ConsoleDestination is constructed with the host and port the runtime binds and accepts an injectable write callable and answer path, so the answer command it prints points at the bind actually serving the answer path.
